description: Observatory regression limits: all 15 areas use runtime architecture. Total build measured at 3.43 MB after replacing palace bakes; 4.3 MB cap prevents retired assets re-entering the release, with headroom for the optional, dynamically-imported three/webgpu chunk (~162 KB gzip) added alongside the WebGL2 fallback renderer. Source media is streamed and measured separately. Startup JS rose to ~220 KB gzip with the palace's second pass (terrain, stairs, the plaque loader and the portal's intent and shader); the cap is 230 KB. On 2026-09-17 the club and phone dock brought main to 230.3 KB, and the grove-wide controls (point, glide, frame, the plan of rooms; their bodies load on demand, their bindings and the Guide's shared move do not) added 2.6 KB more: startup is ~232.9 KB against a cap of 234 KB, and all JS ~703 KB (the lazy glide, framing, map and repository-model chunks) against 706 KB. Later on 2026-09-17 the club floor's stream added its lazy chunks (the way back from silence in the exhibit player, the sound gate, the beat follower, the door curtains): all JS ~709 KB against a cap of 712 KB; startup is unchanged. The desktop and tablet rail (one panel column for the guide, sources, who is here, the chat and frame timing, #55) adds ~1.9 KB to startup and ~1.2 KB to all JS: startup ~235.1 KB against a cap of 237 KB, all JS ~710.4 KB against 714 KB. phototroph's room (#65) adds its lit and dark floors' copy in eight languages to the lazily loaded label chunks and the clock-follow helper: all JS ~715.0 KB against 718 KB; startup is unchanged. The model exhibit kind (a glb on a plinth, 2026-09-17) leaves the startup cap alone (its hanging schema and the world's branch add ~0.2 KB: startup ~235.8 KB against 237 KB). It lazily adds ~3 KB for the model chunk (its placement, and the environment map its materials reflect, built only from classes already in the startup three chunk) and 7.2 KB for three's meshopt decoder, fetched only when a model bundle uses EXT_meshopt_compression (the bundler's answer to a refused Draco glb): with phototroph's room, all JS ~726.3 KB against a cap of 729 KB. The club's two garden courts and their straight, gentler flights (2026-09-17) add their eight-language copy to the lazy label chunks: all JS ~730.1 KB against 733 KB; startup ~236.1 KB against 237 KB. quantumflow's east wing and the rebuilt plan of rooms (2026-09-17) add 10.9 KB to all JS, of which 7.6 KB is the six rooms' copy in eight languages spread across the eight lazily loaded label chunks — no visitor fetches more than their own, so the cost to one of them is ~0.9 KB. The plan itself grows 1.7 KB (floors clustered from the room heights, the picker, pan and zoom, and the menu grouped by area), and it is lazy too: it loads when L or the Map button is first pressed. The wing's six rooms in mansion.json add 0.4 KB to startup and its finish 0.1 KB to the observatory chunk: startup ~236.6 KB against a cap of 237 KB, and all JS ~741.0 KB against 744 KB. Hanging quantumflow's twenty exhibits (2026-09-18) adds 23.4 KB to all JS and 1.6 KB to startup: the captions are twenty more entries in each of the eight lazily loaded label chunks, so a visitor fetches one language of them and not eight, and the hangings themselves are mansion.json, which is in the startup chunk. Startup ~238.2 KB against a cap of 240 KB, all JS ~764.4 KB against 768 KB. The same text and hangings take the whole build to ~4.33 MB against a 4.4 MB cap; the exhibits' own bytes are on the media host and are measured separately, so what grew here is the eight languages of wall text, not the models or the tapes. The hall's two cats (2026-09-18) cost 24.8 KB gzip, in two parts. 20.9 KB is the cats themselves — the vendored body and brain and their nineteen generated clips — and it is lazy: the chunk loads with the hall, so a visitor who never walks in never fetches it. The other 3.9 KB is three.module growing from 143.2 to 147.0 KB, because skinned animation keeps classes (SkinnedMesh, Skeleton, AnimationMixer) that nothing in the palace used before; three is in the startup chunk, so that part is unavoidable while the cats are skinned. Nothing of theirs is imported at module scope from main.ts or world.ts — the room id rides on the built world and the frame loop reuses one visitor object — so startup grows by three's classes and nothing else; an earlier draft that imported the cats' room id from cats.ts put the whole package in startup and cost 41 KB instead. The .glb beside the vendored source is that package's exported form for other consumers and is never imported here, so it is in git and not in the build. Startup ~242.2 KB against a cap of 244 KB, all JS ~789.4 KB against 792 KB, and the whole build ~4.40 MB against a 4.45 MB cap.
